messages:
Daniel Lee: hey everyone, onboarding question — my local compose brings up Postgres but my app can't connect: \"could not connect to server: No such file or directory\". I'm mounting ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data and using POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env. I'm on macbook m1, Docker Desktop. Any quick checks?

Priya Sharma: welcome Daniel! :wave: that error usually means the client is trying to use a unix socket instead of TCP. Are you connecting to localhost:5432 from the app or using a socket path?

Daniel Lee: app env has DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:devpass@localhost:5432/appdb. I can psql into the container with docker exec -it project_db_1 psql -U postgres so server is up. From host I get the socket error.

Omar Reyes: if you're running the app on host (not in a container) and trying to connect via localhost, ensure Postgres is published to host network in compose: 

```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:14
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: devpass
```

Omar Reyes: otherwise the container has its own network and host won't see it. Also macOS socket error sometimes comes from libpq preferring sockets if host is empty or set to ":". Double-check the DSN.

Daniel Lee: ah I did not expose ports because I thought compose network would handle it when app is another service. But currently my app runs locally (outside docker) — so yes need ports. Quick question: is bind mount ok on m1? I've seen random file perms and reinit issues.

Priya Sharma: bind mounts on mac can be flaky. Recommend a named volume for production-like persistence, and bind mount only migrations/sql. If you need host psql files for debugging, mount a separate ./sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d but beware those only run on empty data dir.

Nina Park: another trick: set PGDATA to a subdir to avoid initdb permission problems: PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata. Example: 

```yaml
environment:
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD: devpass
  PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
volumes:
  - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
volumes:
  pgdata:
```

Nina Park: If you must bind mount, run: sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata so postgres can write on host.

Daniel Lee: ok exposing port fixed the socket error when app runs on host. Thanks! One follow-up: I want to run the frontend in docker-compose as well. Then the app would be a service and not need ports. Any gotchas putting both in compose?

Omar Reyes: stack them in same compose project and use service name as host: DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:devpass@db:5432/appdb (where db is the service name). If you switch to that, you don't need ports. Remember to update migrations volume so both services can access if needed.

Priya Sharma: also watch for docker-compose v2 vs v1 env interpolation differences and the compose CLI on Apple Silicon. If you hit slow filesystem slowness for bind mounts, try using :delegated or :cached mount options (macOS), or use a named volume to avoid chokepoints.

InfraBot: Note: docs/setup.md updated with a short note on Postgres host vs container access and macOS bind-mount tips (link: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/setup.md) :white_check_mark:

Daniel Lee: great, that solves it. I'll switch to named volume for data and keep migrations bound for now. Appreciate the quick help everyone! :raised_hands:
